Results.ReviewText: This is the third Weber we have owned in 25 years. I liked the smaller size of this grill and the wide open look. I like where they moved the ignition module and battery, so water can't enter it. We have owned for about 2.5 years, the cross ignition pipe rusted and the flavor bars are rusted out. Results.ReviewText: I bought this at the end of 2019, so I got a little off since it was "last year's model". I've always owned Weber grills and they last a long time. What's nice about the "new ones" is that they come with a ten -(10) warranty on everything! Nobody else offers that type of warranty .  The burners are great (no dead spots) and it lights up every time (it better!) The only complaint I have is with the "Ivory color" I got.  There's "burn marks" coming out of the top seams of the lid of the grill. They don't look good at all and I'm not sure if it's affecting the "grilling aspect" of the grill. Overall, it's a great grill.

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: Things change. Products will never stay the same, so I expected the Weber grill to be a little different than the one I bought 20 years ago. It now has an electric starter, which is easier to use, but it may not hold up over the long road. The ones in the "showroom" had a few bends and rips just from demonstrations. Basic construction appears more balanced than before. This makes it easier to move if needed. Cleaning also seems easier as the two side shelves are more resistant to various spills and potential grime build up. Having the thermostat in the center makes more sense than the one on the side in my previous unit. It is clear and easy to read. I reluctantly gave up my old one, but now that I have this newer model, it was the right decision. Cooking is quicker, easier, and more predictable due to the even heat distribution.

So my 2002 Weber Genesis Silver grill was starting to show its age and this grill was an option for me as a work anniversary gift. I guess I was expecting a downgrade vs my 2002 Genesis but that was not what I got. my 2002 is not dead but took up new residence in Florida at my fishing cabin.    What an upgrade for that house as well.

vs cheap grills I grew up with, the webers can keep a constant temp of 350 to 450 in spite of wind and cold.    My first meal on the spirit was a pork loin cooked with indirect heat on a 40 degree day with a tank that was in the last 1/8th of fuel.     Makes grilling a joy.
